answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A prism delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A zenith check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A pearl penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 4548 identities need 4548 bonds of 69 tokens, 35287 dollars of hardware and 38 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
